papers_read.title_as_printed: Predicting the progression of mild cognitive impairment based on fine-grained and spatiotemporal features of MRI (Hu et al., Biomed Signal Process Control 2025)
An end-to-end multimodal 3D CNN framework with multi-level features for the prediction of mild cognitive impairment (Zhang et al., Knowledge-Based Systems 2023)

what_each_reports.P-122: pMCI vs sMCI (MCI progression) from two-time-point longitudinal structural MRI, ADNI, 275 subjects / 823 longitudinal samples: accuracy 84.74%, AUC 0.8587, sens 83.33%, spec 82.27% (Table 3/5); six-fold CV mean ACC 84.28% (+/-1.65), AUC 0.8599 (Table 2). Internal validation only.
what_each_reports.P-72: The 94.61% the record cites is AD vs NC (215 AD + 246 NC) from baseline sMRI grey matter + FDG-PET. Its sMCI vs pMCI (3-year conversion) result is 77.19% accuracy, AUC 0.755 (Table 5) / 75.56 (Table 7), sens 68.18%. Internal validation only.

quantity_a: Accuracy for pMCI vs sMCI, ADNI, longitudinal (two time points) structural MRI only, internal subject-independent split plus six-fold CV
quantity_b: As cited by the record: accuracy for AD vs NC, ADNI, baseline sMRI GM + FDG-PET. P-72's actual T2 quantity: accuracy for sMCI vs pMCI (3-year conversion) from baseline sMRI + FDG-PET
incompatible_if_same: No. The record's pair sets an AD-vs-NC accuracy against a pMCI-vs-sMCI accuracy, so these are different comparisons. Even on the matching T2 task (84.74% vs 77.19%) the results are two methods reporting different scores. Neither paper claims an ordering the other refutes. In fact P-122 lists P-72's own sMCI/pMCI row (Zhang et al. [21] 2023: 77.19 / 68.18 / 81.86 / 0.7556) in its comparison table and says it improves on it, so both results are presented as true.

gates.task: mismatch for the cited value: P-72's 94.61% is AD vs NC, not T2. The T2 results of the two papers do match as a task.
gates.dataset_family: match: both ADNI (possible subject overlap, recorded as non-independence)
gates.modality_family: mismatch: P-122 is longitudinal structural MRI only; P-72 is multimodal sMRI grey matter + FDG-PET. No waiver on record.

endpoint_and_metric: incompatible for the cited pair: AD-vs-NC diagnosis vs MCI progression. Both report accuracy. P-72 defines conversion at 3 years; P-122 cites a three-year pMCI horizon but gives no explicit conversion window for its own labels.
performance_validity: flag does not apply: no result reaches 0.97 (P-72 AD vs NC AUC 0.947; P-122 AUC 0.8587)
independence: Both draw on ADNI, so subject overlap is possible. No shared authors (Henan University vs Sichuan University groups).
grounds: The record's claim_b misreads P-72: 94.61% is its AD vs NC accuracy, not a T2 (MCI progression) result.
On the matching T2 task, P-72 reports 77.19% and P-122 reports 84.74%. P-122 tabulates P-72's 77.19% row as prior work it improves on, so the two papers do not disagree.
The modality gate also fails (sMRI-only longitudinal vs sMRI+FDG-PET), and there is no waiver on record.

record_defects: claim_b 'P-72: 94.61% AD on T2' is wrong: 94.61% is AD vs NC. P-72's T2 (sMCI vs pMCI) accuracy is 77.19%.
modality_family 'structural_mri' / modality_family_equal 'Yes' is wrong: P-72 is sMRI grey matter + FDG-PET.
task_equal 'Yes' holds only if P-72's T2 result is used, but the record cites the AD-vs-NC figure.
resolution_note 'Metric type unclear: Acc / Unknown' is wrong: both values are plainly accuracy.
The bridging-evidence list is generic ('comparable task/dataset family') and names no condition that separates the two results.
what_would_change_the_verdict: Nothing on these two documents. Even the corrected T2 pair is sMRI-only longitudinal vs sMRI+PET baseline, and P-122 itself reports P-72's number as a lower prior result rather than as a contradiction.
